premise: When my brother died, his will split his $290,000 remote fishing camp equally between me and his widow, but my sister-in-law forged a quitclaim deed transferring my half to her for $1, then sold the entire property to a developer for $310,000; I tracked down the original survey and signature samples, proved the forgery, and the court voided the sale—now I own the camp outright, run it as a women’s angler retreat called ‘Reel Justice Lodge,’ and every quarter I mail my sister-in-law a profit statement with a handwritten note: ‘Thanks for the donation.’
